answers: CBS is scrapping its Early Show team, replacing co-hosts Harry Smith and Maggie Rodriguez with the anchors of the show's Saturday edition, Chris Wragge and Erica Hill. Other more minor players also are leaving in the switch, which takes place early next year, the LA Times reports. The show has been consistently stuck in third place, well behind Today and Good Morning America. Smith, who survived the last major overhaul of the show in 2002, will stick with the network as Katie Couric's main backup on the CBS Evening News, notes AP. Click here for more.

CBS News has undergone a major overhaul of its morning news program, "The Early Show," by replacing its long-standing co-hosts and weather forecaster with a new team. The changes, effective January 3, include the replacement of co-hosts Harry Smith and Maggie Rodriguez with Chris Wragge and Erica Hill, who have been co-anchors of the Saturday edition of the show since 2008. The network has also replaced weather forecaster Dave Price with Marysol Castro, formerly of ABC's "Good Morning America" weekend edition, and added Jeff Glor as the regular news reader.

Harry Smith, who had the longest tenure on the show, will remain at CBS as a news reporter and primary substitute for Katie Couric's evening newscast, "Face the Nation," and "Sunday Morning." Maggie Rodriguez, who briefly filled in for Smith last year, will have her new role determined by the network. Dave Price, who had previously filmed human interest reports, was recently challenged to earn his way back to New York City with only $50 and a phone.

The decision to overhaul the team was made by CBS News President Sean McManus, who believes the new team will help the show grow. The show has consistently ranked behind NBC's "Today" and ABC's "Good Morning America" in ratings. Executive producer David Friedman emphasized that the new team has the right energy and chemistry to improve the show's performance.

The changes were unexpected, with little prior indication of the shift, despite the show's recent change in executive producer. Some critics, like television critic David Bianculli, noted the suddenness of the changes and suggested it may have been a sign of desperation. However, McManus and Friedman remain optimistic about the new team's potential to enhance the show's appeal and ratings.

In addition to the changes in the "Early Show," there was a technical error on a Yahoo! page, which redirected users to an error message, prompting them to check the URL or use the search function. This incident highlights the importance of website maintenance and user experience in online platforms.

Overall, the news highlights both the dynamic nature of media programming and the challenges faced by networks in maintaining viewer engagement and ratings in a competitive landscape.
